summary.headline: School Committee reviews favorable $2.8 million Neary roof bids, a $165,000 feasibility contract for school building options, and staff laptop leasing.
summary.summary: The Southborough School Committee recognized ten retiring district staff members and received end-of-year school updates from principals. Officials reported that bids for the Neary Elementary School roof replacement came in at roughly $2.8 million, substantially below the $4.5 million appropriation, with construction beginning in late June. The committee also discussed a newly executed $165,000 feasibility study contract with Tappé Architects for elementary facilities planning, reviewed a proposed four-year lease for staff MacBooks, and approved year-end budget transfers.

topics.title: Recognition of district retirees
topics.summary: The superintendent and committee recognized ten retiring district educators and support professionals, representing over 200 collective years of service to Southborough public schools. Honorees included Finn School Principal Clayton Ryan and Neary Elementary Principal Kathleen Valenti, along with several longtime classroom teachers and educational support personnel.
key_details: Finn School Principal Clayton Ryan retired after serving the district since 1999 and as school administrator since 2012.
Neary Elementary School Principal Kathleen Valenti retired after leading the school since 2014.

Other recognized retirees included teachers Julie Perrault and Katrina Foley, tutor Jody Baum, and educational support professionals Lori Caccavaro, Diana Posk, Kathleen Riley, Maureen Sullivan-Alves, and Lorraine Muench.
The committee recessed briefly to celebrate with the retirees.
topics.outcome: Informational recognition; no formal action taken.

topics.title: Principals end-of-year reports
topics.summary: Principals from Finn, Woodward, Neary, and Trottier schools presented highlights from end-of-year activities across the district. Highlights included the annual Algonquin Senior Stroll visiting elementary classrooms, expanding school therapy dog programs, spring concerts, middle school fine arts events, and student STEM initiatives.
key_details: Finn School held its Grade 1 concert and celebrated over a dozen community seniors who volunteer regularly in classrooms.
Woodward School welcomed Archie, a trained therapy dog partnered with a staff member, and hosted a Memorial Day concert with Southborough veterans.
Neary School engaged 196 students across bands, chorus, and orchestra, and hosted a fourth-grade STEM unit with the U.S. Army Natick Soldier Center.
Trottier Middle School held Greek and Roman Day, recorded its Big Band at WICN in Worcester, and hosted a multicultural fair representing 34 international flags.

topics.title: Elementary School Building Committee update
topics.summary: The chair of the Elementary School Building Committee reported that a $165,000 contract with Tappé Architects was officially executed to lead the feasibility study and schematic design phase for elementary school facilities. School Committee members stressed the need to adhere to tight timelines to present options to voters at a potential fall Special Town Meeting and emphasized keeping district administration actively involved in committee meetings.
key_details: A $165,000 feasibility and schematic design contract with Tappé Architects was executed on June 10.
The building committee plans to schedule its initial working meetings with Tappé Architects within the next one to two weeks.
Committee members discussed targeting the fall Special Town Meeting to present building options to the town.
School Committee member Roger Challen raised concern over district administration attendance at recent building committee sessions and urged tight coordination.
School Committee Chair Chelsea Malinowski noted that the Select Board must soon establish the fall Town Meeting date to avoid scheduling conflicts.
topics.outcome: Update accepted; initial meetings with architects planned for mid-to-late June.
topics.why_it_matters: The feasibility study evaluates future elementary school construction and renovation options that will ultimately go before town voters for major capital funding.

topics.title: Staff technology four-year lease proposal
topics.summary: The superintendent presented a plan recommended by the technology director to enter a four-year lease for approximately 103 to 105 staff Apple MacBooks. The district's current teacher laptops are six to eight years old and were purchased refurbished, leading to mounting maintenance issues.
key_details: The proposal covers 103 to 105 new Apple laptops for teachers and professional staff.
The lease costs roughly $20,000 annually over four years, fitting within the district's existing $25,000 annual technology line item without increasing the budget.
The agreement includes four years of technical support, device management, and warranty coverage.
At lease end, the district can buy out the devices for $1 each or use Apple's trade-in buyback program.
Older devices that remain functional will be redeployed to support personnel and students.
topics.outcome: Discussion only; proposed lease will be funded through already approved operating funds.
topics.why_it_matters: Ensures school faculty have functional modern technology while establishing a predictable four-year replacement cycle within existing taxpayer-funded operating budgets.

topics.title: Neary School roof project update
topics.summary: The assistant superintendent presented results from the competitive bidding process for the Neary Elementary School roof replacement. Combined low bids totaled approximately $2.8 million, well below the $4.5 million appropriation approved at Town Meeting, with construction slated to begin in late June.
key_details: Total low bids for general contracting and filed sub-bids (plumbing, HVAC, and electrical) totaled approximately $2.8 million.
Voters previously authorized borrowing of up to $4.5 million for the project.
A pre-construction meeting with the general contractor, subcontractors, and school administration is scheduled for Friday morning.
Work is targeted to begin in late June, with 85% to 90% completion anticipated before school opens in late August.
The district plans informational updates to incoming fourth- and fifth-grade families in mid-July and around August 1.
topics.outcome: Project moving into construction late June; contract includes a change order contingency reserve.
topics.why_it_matters: A major capital roofing project is proceeding nearly $1.7 million under its authorized appropriation while minimizing disruption to returning elementary students.

topics.title: Relocation of Summer Extended Day Program
topics.summary: Due to construction on the Neary Elementary roof over the summer, the Southborough Extended Day Program (SEDP) summer program is relocating to Finn Elementary School. Administration noted that adjustments have been made to accommodate older children and all enrolled families have been informed.
key_details: SEDP Summer Fun program relocated from Neary School to Finn School for the summer.
Programming begins after the July 4 holiday.

topics.title: Superintendent enrollment report
topics.summary: Superintendent Martineau reviewed current enrollment projections, clarifying that Finn School will run seven sections of kindergarten and seven sections of first grade next school year. The district is currently in the process of hiring a kindergarten teacher and fourth-grade teacher.
key_details: Finn School will have seven sections of kindergarten and seven sections of grade one.
Postings for open elementary teaching roles are underway with strong candidate pools.

topics.title: FY26 budget transfers and year-end financial report
topics.summary: The director of finance and operations presented the May 31 general fund budget report showing district expenditures of just over $19 million and encumbrances of $5.29 million, leaving a balance of $147,000 (0.59% of the operational budget). The committee approved line-item budget transfers to cover over-expended function codes in administrative technology, athletics, and custodial salaries driven by substitute staffing, utilities, and collaborative tuition pressures.
key_details: District had an available balance of $147,000 as of May 31.
Available balance dropped by $74,000 from the prior month due to year-end substitute staffing, utilities, and collaborative tuition costs.
Budget transfers were required to rebalance overages in Administrative Technology, Athletics, and Custodial Salaries.
topics.outcome: The committee voted 5-0 to approve the FY26 line-item transfers and accept the monthly General Fund report until audited.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee reviewed routine administrative items including May warrants and payrolls, the personnel report, open meeting minutes, and the public release of past executive session minutes before entering executive session.
key_details: Approved accounts payable warrants and two payroll runs for the month of May.
Personnel report noted appointments, retirements, and the resignation of a Woodward art teacher.
Approved open meeting minutes from May 13, 2026.
Approved the public release of executive session minutes from September 17, 2024; August 7, 2025; September 10, 2025; October 8, 2025; and November 12, 2025.
Voted by roll call to enter executive session regarding collective bargaining strategy and security personnel/devices, not to reconvene in open session.

topics.title: Revolving accounts update
topics.summary: Finance staff presented projected year-end fund balances across the district's revolving accounts, noting that all four programs remain financially stable. Staff also explained that the preschool revolving account will split from the Northborough-Southborough regional account into independent town accounts starting in the upcoming fiscal year.
key_details: Projected year-end balances include Food Services at $112,000, Facility Rentals at $23,000, Extended Day at $563,000, and Preschool at $102,000.
Facility rental revenues will be replenished next fiscal year by leases from Assabet Valley Collaborative, Northborough, and the regional district.
An estimated $85,000 spent prior to town meeting approval could not be charged back to the facility revolving fund.
Northborough and Southborough preschool revolving funds are officially separating for the upcoming school year.

votes.motion: Vote to accept the FY26 monthly General Fund report as of May 31, 2026 until audited and approve the overexpended function codes listed.
Vote to approve warrants and payrolls as presented in the packet.
Vote to release executive session minutes from September 17, 2024; August 7, 2025; September 10, 2025; October 8, 2025; and November 12, 2025.

Vote to enter executive session under M.G.L. c. 30A, Section 21(a)(3) to discuss strategy regarding collective bargaining with Southborough Teachers Association Unit C (administrative assistants and educational support professionals), and Section 21(a)(4) to discuss security personnel, devices, or strategies, not to reconvene in open session.
